theater: 昆明首義與川南湘西戰線

battle.name: 護國戰爭
battle.theater: 昆明首義與川南湘西戰線
battle.brief: 1915年12月25日，蔡鍔與唐繼堯、李烈鈞在昆明宣布雲南獨立，護國軍出師川南、黔東與湘西，各省先後響應，戰事延續到翌年7月。卡面德製M1888步槍是滇軍裝備骨幹，射程與火力構成攻勢核心；北洋軍同樣大量配備此型槍，敵我同口徑彈藥可以互通，前線補給與火力強弱直接決定川南攻守的取捨。

kit.name: M1888步槍
kit.history: 德國1888年研製的栓式步槍，清末引進，廣泛配用於中國內戰。

countries: 這場戰爭是中華民國成立後第一次大規模的內戰，交戰雙方都在中國境內，卻各自代表不同的政治主張。北洋方面以北京大總統袁世凱為中心，依靠北洋新軍的建制部隊：陸軍第三師師長曹錕所部先後入湘鄂，第七師師長張敬堯率師入川，另有第二師、第十八師等師制單位，以及各地巡警、治安軍與地方武裝；指揮上由大總統府經參謀總長、陸軍總長段祺瑞逐級下達，雲南督軍唐繼堯、四川督軍陳慶新、廣東督軍龍濟光、湖南督軍湯蓍銘、廣西督軍陸榮廷等地方當局各守一方，電令與命令互相矛盾，統一指揮並不順暢。護國方面組建護國軍，總司令部設於昆明，總司令蔡鍔，副總司令唐繼堯、李烈鈞，下轄第一軍至第三軍等序列：第一軍以滇軍為主力，第二軍由李烈鈞統率，第三軍由唐繼堯直接指揮，其後續有擴編，第四軍為貴州方向、第五軍為湖南方向、第六軍為廣東方向、第七軍為陝西方向的部隊。各省宣布獨立的時間先後不一，廣西與湖南在三月中旬，廣東在四月十一日，貴州與陝西在五月，浙江、江蘇等地亦陸續響應，名義上的一致背書與實際上各行其是同時存在。整場衝突並非單純的南北對壘，而是北京中央、地方軍閥與各省護國軍彼此糾纏的三方角力，同時發生在歐洲大戰正酣、日本提出二十一條的國際背景之下。
countriesEn: This war was the first large-scale civil war after the founding of the Republic of China. Both sides fought on Chinese soil while representing different political programmes. On the Beiyang side the centre was President Yuan Shikai in Beijing, and the government relied on the organised formations of the New Army: the 3rd Division under General Cao Kun moved into Hunan and western Hubei, the 7th Division under Zhang Jingyao entered Sichuan, and further divisional units such as the 2nd and 18th Divisions, together with provincial police forces, peace-preservation troops and local armed bands, were committed. Command ran from the presidential office through Chief of the General Staff and War Minister Duan Qirui down the chain of command, while provincial authorities such as Governor Tang Jiyao of Yunnan, Chen Qingxin of Sichuan, Long Jiguang of Guangdong, Tang Shaoming of Hunan and Lu Rongting of Guangxi each held their own ground; telegrams and orders from the centre contradicted one another and unified direction was never smooth. On the other side the National Protection Army was organised with its general headquarters at Kunming: Commander-in-chief Cai E, with Tang Jiyao and Li Liejun as vice-commanders-in-chief, and beneath them a series running from the 1st Army onward. The 1st Army was built on the Yunnan troops, the 2nd was commanded by Li Liejun, the 3rd by Tang Jiyao himself; the force was later enlarged, with the 4th Army operating towards Guizhou, the 5th towards Hunan, the 6th towards Guangdong and the 7th towards Shaanxi. The provinces declared independence at different moments, Guangxi and Hunan in the middle of March, Guangdong on 11 April, Guizhou and Shaanxi in May, with Zhejiang, Jiangsu and others answering in turn, so that nominal agreement and separate action existed at the same time. The conflict was not a clean north-against-south war but a three-way entanglement among the Beijing centre, the regional warlords and the provincial National Protection armies, and it unfolded against the background of the European Great War and of Japan's Twenty-One Demands.
people: 蔡鍔是這場戰爭的樞紐。他字松坡，湖南邵陽人，留學日本，早年主持雲南陸軍與雲南陸軍講武堂的整頓，把滇軍按德式操典與德造武器編訓；1913年調任北京，任袁世凱的幕僚，兩人交誼頗深。袁世凱推行帝制後，蔡鍔表面恭順，1915年10月藉故離京，經天津、日本、越南轉入雲南，11月15日抵達昆明，與唐繼堯、李烈鈞及滇軍將領秘密策劃起義。12月25日起義當日，他出任護國軍總司令，通電反對帝制；此後他抱病在前線督戰，川南棉花坡一役的攻勢即由他策劃，其肺病亦在這一階段迅速惡化，4月間東渡日本就醫，11月8日病逝於神戶，靈柩後運回湖南，安葬衡陽。唐繼堯是雲南本省的主事者，起義時以雲南都督兼護國軍第三軍軍長的身分坐鎮昆明，主持出師、糧餉與後方秩序，蔡鍔病重離境後由他接掌護國軍最高指揮權，事後出任雲南都督，統治雲南多年。李烈鈞是江西人，二次革命時任江西都督，1915年在上海策劃反袁未遂，12月潛回雲南，任護國軍第二軍總司令，率江西與外省入滇的部隊作戰。北洋方面的關鍵人物包括：曹錕，以第三師為主力在湖南、鄂西方向對抗護國軍；張敬堯，率第七師入川，是川南棉花坡與瀘州方向的主要對手；段祺瑞，掌參謀總長與陸軍總長，調度北洋各師入湘入川，袁世凱死後出任國務總理。地方方面，陸榮廷宣布廣西獨立後成為兩廣方向的支柱，譚延闓在湖南宣布獨立並出任護國軍第五軍總司令，龍濟光在廣東宣布獨立卻拒絕退出廣州，劉顯世、陳樹藩分別在貴州、陝西響應起義。護國軍內部還有各師、旅的指揮官，以及大量雲南陸軍講武堂出身、隨軍作戰的教官與下級軍官，正是這批人把德式操典帶到滇南與川南前線。
peopleEn: Cai E was the pivot of the entire war. He styled himself Songpo, was born in Shaoyang, Hunan, and had studied in Japan; in his earlier career he reorganised the Yunnan army and the Yunnan Military Academy, training and equipping the provincial troops on the German model and with German arms. He was transferred to Beijing in 1913 and served at Yuan Shikai's side, and the two were on personally close terms. Once Yuan began pushing for the monarchy, Cai feigned obedience, slipped out of Beijing in October 1915, travelled by way of Tianjin, Japan and Vietnam into Yunnan and reached Kunming on 15 November, where he and Tang Jiyao, Li Liejun and the Yunnan commanders worked out the timing, place and order of departure for the rising. On 25 December, the day the rising began, he took command as commander-in-chief of the National Protection Army and issued the denunciation of the monarchy. From then on he directed operations at the front despite his illness; the offensives at Mianhuapo in southern Sichuan were planned by him, and his lung disease worsened sharply during that phase. He sailed to Japan for treatment in April, died at Kobe on 8 November, and his coffin was later carried back to Hunan and buried at Hengyang. Tang Jiyao was the man of the province itself: at the rising he was governor of Yunnan and commander of the 3rd Army, and from Kunming he directed the advance, the pay and the rear-area administration, taking over the highest command of the National Protection Army when Cai E's illness forced him abroad, and afterwards governing Yunnan for many years. Li Liejun, a Jiangxi man who had been governor of Jiangxi during the Second Revolution, failed in an anti-Yuan plot in Shanghai in 1915 and slipped back to Yunnan in December to command the 2nd Army with the troops from Jiangxi and other provinces. On the Beiyang side the decisive figures were Cao Kun, who fought in Hunan and western Hubei with the 3rd Division; Zhang Jingyao, whose 7th Division entered Sichuan and who was the main opponent around Mianhuapo and Luzhou; and Duan Qirui, who as chief of the general staff and war minister moved the northern divisions into Hunan and Sichuan and became premier after Yuan's death. Regionally, Lu Rongting became the pillar of the southern front after declaring Guangxi independent, Tan Yankai declared Hunan independent and headed the 5th Army, Long Jiguang declared Guangdong independent yet refused to leave Guangzhou, and Liu Xianshi and Chen Shufan answered the rising in Guizhou and Shaanxi. Inside the National Protection Army stood divisional and brigade commanders together with a large body of academy-trained instructors and junior officers, and it was precisely these men who carried German drill and German rifles down to the fronts in southern Yunnan and southern Sichuan.
kits: 卡面的M1888步槍是德國1888年定型的七點九二毫米栓式步槍，槍管外套木質或帆布套筒，槍身約四公斤有餘，配五發排夾，栓塞後拉供彈，標尺有效射程約八百公尺，槍口初速與後座力足以讓射手在三四百公尺上維持精度。它在護國戰爭裡的位置十分明確：既是滇軍步兵的制式槍，也是北洋新軍多個師的制式槍，兩條軍火來源都指向德國，同型槍同口徑，於是前線出現一種奇特局面——敵我對射用的是同一種彈藥，誰的後方供應線更穩，誰就能把火力優勢兌現成戰果。中國自製的仿德造步槍，例如湖北槍炮廠出產的漢陽造，也以德國一八八八年式為母型，口徑同為七點九二毫米，同樣出現在北洋軍與各路地方部隊手中。滇軍是國內最早成批引進德造七點九二毫米步槍的部隊之一，蔡鍔在雲南期間多次向德國訂購步槍與機槍，總數各記說法從數千至上萬支不等，相差頗大。步槍之外，滇軍裝備機槍，重機槍以德造水冷式為主，輕機槍數量有限；砲兵以七五公分野砲與山砲為骨幹，另有少量迫擊砲；尚有騎兵部隊，軍馬多為北方購進的蒙古馬與雲南本地矮馬，能適應山地而衝鋒力不足；另有數量不多的舊式步槍與梭標、大刀作為補充。北洋方面，新制各師同樣以德造步槍為主，部分師已換裝日造三十年式步槍，地方武裝與舊軍仍用仿德造七九式與更舊的槍械，口徑七點九二、六五、六八毫米混雜，彈藥難以統一發放。糧秣方面，護國軍主要依賴滇越鐵路與馬幫挑夫，從雲南腹地到川南前線縱深逾千里，沿途徵集，缺口長期存在；運輸仍以馬匹、人力挑擔與鐵路車輛為主，汽車極少，滇越鐵路河口至昆明一段坡度大、運力有限，成為整條補給線的瓶頸。
kitsEn: The M1888 on the card face is the 7.92 mm bolt-action rifle standardised by Germany in 1888, with the barrel wrapped in a wooden or canvas jacket, a service weight of a little over four kilograms, a five-round stripper clip, a bolt-action feed and a sighting range of roughly eight hundred metres; its muzzle velocity and recoil are enough to let a shooter hold accuracy at three or four hundred metres. Its place in the National Protection War is perfectly clear: it was the standard rifle of the Yunnan infantry and equally the standard rifle of several Beiyang New Army divisions, and both lines of supply pointed back to Germany, so that the same model and the same calibre met on the front in a peculiar way, with the two sides firing at each other using identical ammunition. Whoever kept his rear supply line steadier was the one who could convert a superiority in firepower into actual results on the ground. Chinese-made copies of the German design, such as the Hanyang rifle turned out by the Hubei Arsenal, also took the German 1888 pattern as their parent, shared the same 7.92 mm calibre, and appeared in Beiyang and local hands alike. The Yunnan army was among the first units in the country to take delivery of German 7.92 mm rifles in bulk, and during his years in Yunnan Cai E placed repeated orders with German firms for rifles and machine guns; the totals recorded differ widely, from several thousand to more than ten thousand, and the accounts conflict considerably. Beyond rifles, the Yunnan army carried machine guns, the heavy weapon being of German water-cooled type while light machine guns were few; the artillery arm rested on 75 mm field and mountain guns with a small number of mortars; there was also a mounted arm, its animals mostly Mongolian horses bought from the north together with local Yunnan ponies, which could work in the hills but lacked the weight for a charge; and a small quantity of older rifles, spears and big sabres served as auxiliaries. On the Beiyang side the newly organised divisions likewise relied on German rifles, some had already been re-equipped with Japanese Type 30 rifles, and local bands and old units still carried German-pattern 7.9 mm weapons and older types still, so that calibres of 7.92, 6.5 and 6.8 mm were mixed and ammunition could not be issued in a single standard. As for supply, the National Protection Army depended chiefly on the Yunnan-Vietnam railway and on mule trains and porters; the distance from the interior of Yunnan to the front in southern Sichuan ran to more than a thousand li, requisition was carried out along the way, and the shortfall remained a standing problem. Transport was still by horse, human shoulder-pole and railway wagon, with very few motor vehicles, and the steep section of the Yunnan-Vietnam line between Hekou and Kunming limited capacity so severely that it became the bottleneck of the whole supply route.
tactics: 護國軍的作戰可以分成三段。起義與整頓：一九一五年十二月二十五日，昆明城內槍炮聲響起，護國軍依令控制火車站、電報局與城門等要點，封鎖對外電訊，控制滇越鐵路車站，同時整頓部隊、補充彈藥、宣布紀律，把一支剛完成德式整訓的省軍轉為攻勢部隊。進攻次序是三路並進：一路出滇東指向貴州，策應貴州方向倒戈；一路指向廣南、廣西方向，與陸榮廷部呼應；主力沿滇東鐵路與公路向川南推進，目標是敘府與瀘州，把袁軍在西南的據點逐個拔掉。川南的攻防集中在棉花坡一帶，丘陵與溪谷交錯，護國軍以步兵分批投入，散兵線在射界內交替躍進，機槍集中支援，迫擊砲與山砲覆蓋對方陣地；北洋軍依托已築的工事與砲火優勢反擊，雙方在坡地反覆拉鋸，一度短兵相接。側翼與後方，護國軍大量使用夜襲、伏擊與破壞交通的手段，斷北洋軍的糧道與通信，騎兵支隊往來擾亂側後，地方武裝與護國軍配合，令中央軍難以集中兵力。補給線是這場戰爭最脆弱的一環：滇越鐵路是唯一的大宗運輸骨幹，河口至昆明坡度大、運力有限，馬幫與挑夫再補最後數十公里，糧食多靠沿途徵集，前線缺糧缺彈的消息屢見不鮮，蔡鍔因此強調就地籌措與軍紀，試圖以行政手段維持後方。袁世凱去世後，攻勢轉為停戰收束，各路部隊收縮、復員，護國軍的軍事階段在1916年7月結束。
tacticsEn: The conduct of the National Protection Army can be divided into three phases. First the rising and the reorganisation of the force: on 25 December 1915 gunfire and artillery broke out inside Kunming, and by order the National Protection Army seized the railway station, the telegraph office and the city gates, cut outward traffic, controlled the Yunnan-Vietnam line and its stations, and at the same time tidied the units, replenished ammunition, proclaimed discipline and converted a provincial army that had just finished German-style training into an offensive force. Second the order of attack, which went in along three axes: one column out of eastern Yunnan towards Guizhou, in support of the defection there; one towards Guangnan and Guangxi, coordinating with Lu Rongting's troops; and the main body along the eastern Yunnan railway and roads into southern Sichuan, with the object of taking Sifu and Luzhou and knocking out the Beiyang strongholds in the southwest one by one. The fighting in southern Sichuan concentrated around Mianhuapo, where hills and gullies interlock, and the National Protection Army fed in infantry battalion by battalion, skirmish lines advancing in turn within the beaten zone, machine guns massed in support and mortars and mountain guns covering the opposing positions; the Beiyang troops answered from prepared earthworks with the advantage of artillery, and the two sides fought to and fro over the slopes, at moments closing to close range. On the flanks and in the rear the National Protection Army made heavy use of night attacks, ambushes and the cutting of communications, cutting the Beiyang grain and message routes, while mounted detachments worked the rear and local bands cooperated with the army, making it hard for the central forces to concentrate. Supply was the most fragile part of the whole war: the Yunnan-Vietnam railway was the single artery for bulk transport, the stretch from Hekou to Kunming was steep and of limited capacity, mules and porters covered the last tens of kilometres, food was gathered along the line, and reports of hunger and shortage of ammunition at the front were frequent, which is why Cai E pressed for local collection and strict discipline in the hope of holding the rear together by administrative means. After Yuan Shikai's death the offensive turned into an armistice and a gathering up of forces, the various columns contracting and being stood down, and the military phase of the National Protection Army ended in July 1916.
data: 這場戰爭的數字在史料中相當零散，只能把把握較大的寫下。時間上，起義定於1915年12月25日，護國運動的政治階段結束於1916年7月，前後約六個半月。參與省份方面，宣布獨立的省市常見統計為十二個，實際響應的程度差別很大，雲南控制得最完整，廣東宣布獨立而未交出廣州，陝西一省則只有象徵性的響應。兵力方面，護國軍的雲南主力通常記作三個師，約三萬人，各省響應部隊合計之後，各家統計從數萬到七八萬不等；北洋方面調動了曹錕第三師、張敬堯第七師等多個師，加上地方武裝，投入總數從十餘萬到二十餘萬都有記載，數字彼此牴觸，難以核實。地理尺度上，滇軍自昆明出發，最遠推進到川南的瀘州與敘府方向，縱深逾千里；川南一線的主要戰役包括棉花坡、敘州、瀘州等數戰，湘西與黔東方向亦有反覆交鋒。裝備數量同樣存疑：雲南在1909至1911年間多次向德國購進步槍與機槍，總數各說從數千至上萬支不等。傷亡方面，雙方數字普遍誇大而且互相矛盾，可以確定的只是川南、湘西、黔東各線都有成建制的部隊傷亡，各次戰役的損失以千計，具體數目已難追溯。唯一較為確定的是時間跨度與地理範圍：不到七個月，戰線由雲南一隅擴展到滇、黔、川、湘、桂、粵、陝數省之內。
dataEn: The figures for this war are scattered across the sources, and only those that can be held with some confidence can be set down. As to time, the rising is fixed at 25 December 1915 and the political phase of the movement ended in July 1916, a span of about six and a half months. As to the provinces involved, the usual tally of cities and provinces that declared independence is twelve, though the depth of their response varied greatly: Yunnan was controlled most completely, Guangdong declared independence without giving up Guangzhou, and Shaanxi gave only a token response. As to strength, the Yunnan main force of the National Protection Army is usually recorded as three divisions of about thirty thousand men, and once the responding provincial troops are added the totals published run from several tens of thousands to seventy or eighty thousand; on the Beiyang side several divisions were moved, among them Cao Kun's 3rd Division and Zhang Jingyao's 7th Division, and with local armed bands added the figures quoted range from a hundred thousand to more than two hundred thousand, the numbers contradict one another and cannot be checked. As to geography, the Yunnan army set out from Kunming and pushed as far as Luzhou and Sifu in southern Sichuan, a depth of more than a thousand li, the main engagements on that line being Mianhuapo, Sizhou and Luzhou, while the Hunan-western and eastern Guizhou fronts saw repeated fighting. The equipment totals are equally uncertain: between 1909 and 1911 Yunnan bought rifles and machine guns from Germany on several occasions, and the various accounts put the number anywhere from several thousand to more than ten thousand. On casualties the figures published on both sides are plainly exaggerated and mutually contradictory; what can be certain is only that the lines in southern Sichuan, western Hunan and eastern Guizhou each saw whole units suffer losses, and that the cost of the individual actions ran into the thousands, the exact numbers being beyond recovery. The only reasonably firm elements are the span of time and the reach of the theatre: in under seven months the front widened from a corner of Yunnan into Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hunan, Guangxi, Guangdong and Shaanxi.
cause: 護國戰爭的直接起因，是袁世凱推行帝制。一九一五年三月，赴日談判的陸徵祥等接受日本提出的二十一條大部分要求；同年五月日本再度提出要求，日本在中國的擴張由此加深。八月二十日，楊度等人在北京組織籌安會，公開為帝制造勢；十二月十二日，袁世凱在國民黨與立法院議員簇擁下接受推戴，宣布稱帝，定國號中華帝國，改元洪憲，並在文武百官跪拜之下於正殿受賀。帝制的推行在體制上清算共和：解散國會、廢除臨時約法、罷黜南方各省都督、削弱各省軍權，這直接觸動了以軍人為主力的南方省份。孫中山在二次革命失敗後流亡日本，號召倒袁，並策劃上海的暗殺行動；李烈鈞事敗後轉向雲南，與蔡鍔的默契同時形成。蔡鍔與袁世凱原有交誼，但帝制使二人分道，1915年10月他秘密離京，取道日本、越南，11月15日回到昆明，與唐繼堯及滇軍將領商定起義時間、地點與出師序列。更遠的背景是中央與地方的權力矛盾：民國以來北洋軍掌握中央武力，各省軍隊與之互不信任；雲南經蔡鍔整軍、購械後實力上升，與北京的關係更形緊張。國際層面，歐洲大戰自1914年開打，英、俄、日、美各懷打算，一方希望中國政府集中力量應對歐洲局勢，一方希望借中國的內部混亂牟利，這種外部牽制反而給了國內反對派行動空間。上述諸項交疊，護國起義才在1915年底成為可能。
causeEn: The immediate cause of the National Protection War was Yuan Shikai's push for a monarchy. In March 1915 the negotiators sent to Japan, headed by Lu Zhengxiang, accepted most of the Twenty-One Demands; in May Japan submitted fresh demands, and the deepening of Japanese penetration in China followed from that. On 20 August Yang Du and others in Beijing formed the Preparatory Association for Constitutional Monarchy and openly campaigned for the throne; on 12 December Yuan Shikai, pressed forward by members of the National Protection party and of the Legislative Yuan, accepted the acclamation, proclaimed himself emperor, set the title of the Empire of China, changed the era to Hongxian, and received congratulation in the great hall while the civil and military officials knelt. The monarchy was meant to liquidate the republic at the level of institutions: dissolving parliament, abolishing the Provisional Constitution, dismissing the southern provincial governors and curbing the military power of the provinces, which struck directly at the southern provinces whose strength lay in their soldiers. Sun Yat-sen, exiled in Japan after the failure of the Second Revolution, called for the fall of Yuan and organised the assassination attempt in Shanghai; after his own scheme collapsed Li Liejun turned towards Yunnan, at the same time as the understanding between him and Cai E took shape. Cai E and Yuan Shikai had been close, but the monarchy drove them apart; in October 1915 Cai secretly left Beijing, travelled by way of Japan and Vietnam, and on 15 November was back in Kunming, where he and Tang Jiyao and the Yunnan commanders settled the timing, the place and the order of departure of the rising. Further back lies the contradiction of authority between centre and locality: since the founding of the Republic the Beiyang armies had held the central armed power while the provincial troops and the centre distrusted one another, and Yunnan, after Cai E's reorganisation and purchasing, had grown stronger and stood in a tenser relation to Beijing. On the international plane, the European Great War had been running since 1914, and Britain, Russia, Japan and the United States each had their own calculations, one side hoping the Chinese government would concentrate on the European situation and the other hoping to profit from disorder inside China, and this external restraint gave the domestic opposition room to move. Only through the overlap of all these conditions did the National Protection rising become possible at the end of 1915.
impact: 護國運動最直接的結果，是洪憲帝制的瓦解。1916年6月6日袁世凱病逝北京，遺囑仍囑維持帝制，但副總統黎元洪依法律程序於6月7日宣布取消國號、恢復共和，君主制的岔路就此關上。在政治版圖上，護國運動打破了北洋政府的獨裁局面，也把中央與地方的裂痕暴露在全國面前。段祺瑞以討伐護國軍的名義出任國務總理，各省督軍卻多已由護國軍的將領或響應者接掌，於是護國軍解散之後，中央對地方的控制反而更弱，地方軍閥割據的局面自此固定下來。雲南因出力最多、控制雲貴川南最廣，一時居於強勢地位，唐繼堯先後出任雲南都督與貴州、廣東都督；護國軍改組的方案則各方不一，孫中山主張護國軍改組為國民黨，滇軍方面持保留態度，改組最終以各部各自分別裁撤、縮編或改稱國民軍收場，這一分歧延續到護國運動之後仍未完全化解。長遠看，護國運動提供了民國初年反對專制的一個樣本，成為日後護法運動與廣州軍政府的法理與象徵來源，護國二字自此進入國家記憶，各省建立紀念碑與紀念館，蔡鍔被追認為共和象徵，靈柩歸葬衡陽的場面成為民初政治史上少數的民間自發聚合。在軍備與國際局勢上，護國運動前後各省為自保而擴軍，德造一八八八年式步槍大量外流，一部分經護國軍各部之手散入川、黔、湘、粵各地，一部分隨北洋軍與地方武裝分發，內戰的規模與烈度都因此提高；帝制雖亡，二十一條引發的民族不滿卻未解決，其影響在1919年才全面爆發；日本趁歐洲大戰之機擴張在華利益，1917年借對德宣戰出兵中國，護國運動所打開的內外交互動格局，在其後數年間持續發酵。
impactEn: The most immediate outcome of the National Protection movement was the collapse of the Hongxian monarchy. Yuan Shikai died of illness in Beijing on 6 June 1916, and although his will still asked that the monarchy be maintained, the vice-president Li Yuanhong, acting on the legal procedure, proclaimed the cancellation of the imperial title and the restoration of the republic on 7 June, and the road to monarchy was closed for good. In the political map, the movement broke the dictatorship of the Beiyang government and exposed the fissure between centre and locality to the whole country. Duan Qirui became premier in the name of suppressing the National Protection Army, yet the provincial governorships had already gone mostly to the generals or partisans of the movement, so that after the army was dissolved the centre's control over the localities grew weaker and the pattern of regional warlord separatism was fixed. Yunnan, which had borne the brunt and held the widest area across Yunnan, Guizhou and southern Sichuan, stood for a time in the stronger position, and Tang Jiyao served in turn as governor of Yunnan and then of Guizhou and Guangdong. The plan for reorganising the National Protection Army was not agreed: Sun Yat-sen urged that the army be reorganised into the Nationalist Party, the Yunnan side held back, and in the end the reorganisation resolved into the separate disbandment, reduction or renaming of each army as the National Army, a disagreement that was still not fully settled after the movement was over. In the longer run the movement supplied the early Republic with a model of resistance to autocracy, and became the legal and symbolic fountainhead of the later Constitutional Protection movement and the Guangzhou government; the two characters of the National Protection entered the national memory, provinces raised monuments and museums to it, Cai E was canonised as a symbol of the republic, and the scenes attending the return of his coffin to Hengyang became one of the few spontaneous popular gatherings in the political history of the early Republic. As for armament and the international situation, the provinces expanded their armies to protect themselves around the time of the movement, and German 1888-pattern rifles spilled out in quantity, some carried away by the different National Protection armies into Sichuan, Guizhou, Hunan and Guangdong, some distributed with the Beiyang and local armed bands, so that the scale and intensity of civil war rose accordingly. The monarchy had fallen, yet the resentment over the Twenty-One Demands was not resolved and only broke out in full in 1919; and Japan, taking advantage of the European war, extended its interests in China and sent troops into the country in 1917 on the pretext of declaring war on Germany, so that the interaction of domestic upheaval and foreign intervention opened by the National Protection War continued to work itself out for years afterwards.
result: 1915年12月25日昆明起義之後，護國軍以滇軍為骨幹向外推進：1916年初沿滇東線進入貴州方向，2月至3月在川南的棉花坡、敘州、瀘州一線與北洋軍反覆爭奪，3月15日廣西與湖南宣布獨立，4月11日廣東宣布獨立，5月4日貴州、5月5日陝西宣布獨立，浙江、江蘇、山東等地亦先後響應。護國軍一度攻入湘中與黔東，四川督軍陳慶新被推翻，劉湘接任川督。與此同時，護國軍入粵受挫，廣東方面龍濟光宣布獨立卻未退出廣州，護國軍在廣東方向的攻勢停在河源一帶未能得手，這是護國軍戰線上少數沒有進展的方向。六月初袁世凱在北京病逝，6月7日帝制取消，6月下旬各線大規模停火，7月6日段祺瑞出任國務總理，護國軍於7月宣告解散或改組，各路部隊陸續復員、裁撤，戰爭以政治妥協收場，而不是以某一場會戰的勝負收場。結果可以分三層看：袁世凱的帝制計畫徹底失敗，共和形式得以保留；各省護國軍與中央的對抗沒有產出一個能統一全國的替代秩序，反而把地方軍閥的權力坐大，雲南藉此在西南取得相對優勢；而護國軍內部從一開始就缺乏統一指揮與穩定後勤，各軍各自為戰，導致勝利來得比預期快，散得也同樣快。
resultEn: After the rising at Kunming on 25 December 1915 the National Protection Army pushed outward with the Yunnan troops as its backbone: in the opening months of 1916 it entered eastern Guizhou, and between February and March fought repeated contests with the Beiyang army along the Mianhuapo, Sizhou and Luzhou line in southern Sichuan; on 15 March Guangxi and Hunan declared independence, on 11 April Guangdong did the same, Guizhou followed on 4 May and Shaanxi on 5 May, and Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Shandong and others answered in turn. The National Protection armies entered central Hunan and eastern Guizhou, the Sichuan governor Chen Qingxin was overthrown and Liu Xiang took over as governor of Sichuan. At the same time the drive into Guangdong was checked: Long Jiguang declared independence but did not leave Guangzhou, and the National Protection offensive in that direction stalled around Heyuan without success, one of the few sectors on the whole front where the advance failed. In early June Yuan Shikai died of illness in Beijing, the monarchy was cancelled on 7 June, large-scale ceasing of fire followed along every line in late June, Duan Qirui became premier on 6 July, and in July the National Protection Army was either dissolved or reorganised, its columns being stood down and cut in succession. The war thus ended in a political compromise rather than in the decision of any single pitched battle. The result may be read on three levels. Yuan Shikai's plan for a monarchy failed outright and the republican form was preserved; the resistance of the provincial National Protection armies to the centre produced no alternative order capable of uniting the country, but instead confirmed the power of the regional warlords, with Yunnan gaining a relative ascendancy in the southwest; and the National Protection Army lacked unified command and steady logistics from the very beginning, each army fighting its own battle, which is why victory came faster than expected and the dispersal came just as quickly.
